transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: *Looks up from ledger, adjusting spectacles* Ah, good day, sir. You seem... agitated. Is there something I can help you with regarding an order?

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Indeed, there is! I have come to discuss a matter of considerable urgency. The printing plate I recently commissioned has arrived in a state most unsatisfactory. The face is cracked, and the type is smeared beyond redemption! This is entirely unacceptable, and I demand a full replacement and refund of my deposit.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: *Sighs, closing the ledger with a soft thud* Ah, yes. The gentleman with the political pamphlet plate. I recall the order. Unfortunate about the damage, truly. But I'm afraid I must inform you of our shop custom: all engraving orders are final once the plate has left the workshop; the customer bears full risk of transport damage, without exception. We cannot issue a refund or replacement.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: This is preposterous! You would have us believe that the condition of the product is of no concern to you once it has left your establishment? Allow me to remind you, the responsibility for the quality of your craftsmanship does not cease at the threshold of your shop. If your work is faulty, it is your obligation to rectify the situation. This is not merely a matter of profit and loss, but of integrity!

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: *Leans back in the chair, fingers steepled* Sir, with respect, the plate left here in perfect condition. Our apprentice personally inspected it. The risk of transport is clearly stated in our terms, which you agreed to when placing the order. If the carrier was careless, your grievance lies with them, not with us. We fulfilled our contract.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: *Snorts derisively* Contracts, you say? The workers in your shop, your 'apprentices,' no doubt toil under the most deplorable conditions, producing shoddy workmanship, while you absolve yourself of responsibility by hiding behind legalese! You are nothing more than a capitalist profiteer, concerned only with the accumulation of wealth, with no regard for the quality of the work you produce or the satisfaction of your customers! This is the very essence of the bourgeoisie's exploitation of the proletariat!

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: *Raises an eyebrow, a faint, weary smile on his face* A philosopher, are we? My apprentices are well-paid and learn a valuable trade. They take pride in their work. Your plate was not "shoddy." It was damaged in transit. That is a simple fact. If you wish to debate economic theory, I suggest a coffee house. This is a place of business. Our policy stands.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: *Recoils, incensed* You dare to trivialize my concerns with derision? This is not a matter of mere semantics! The condition of the plate reflects directly on the quality of your work. If it was not properly constructed, it would not have succumbed to such damage so easily. This is indicative of deeper issues within your production process. I demand that you take responsibility for your shoddy product! If you will not assist me, I will take my business elsewhere and inform all of my associates of the substandard nature of your work!

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: *Stands up, placing both hands on the counter, voice firm but calm* Sir, I have been patient. The plate was copper, properly annealed and engraved to specification. It could survive a reasonable journey. If it was thrown from a carriage or crushed under a heavier load, that is not a flaw in our craft. Shouting about production processes will not change our custom. You are welcome to take your business elsewhere. As for your associates... *shrugs slightly* we have a long list of satisfied clients. One angry philosopher will not break us. Now, is there anything else pertaining to a *current* order I can assist you with?

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: *Fists clenching at his sides, face flushed with anger* You... You...! This is unconscionable! You have no regard for the needs of the common man, for the principles of fairness and justice! I... I...! This... This is indicative of the inherent contradictions of capitalism! Your... Your exploitation of the working class is... is...! *Steps back, taking a deep, calming breath* I see now that further discussion with you is fruitless. I shall take my complaint to the appropriate authorities, and I shall ensure that your... your... unscrupulous practices are exposed to the public! May your business... may it... suffer!

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: *Nods curtly, opening the ledger again* As you wish, sir. The authorities know our shop and our reputation. Good day to you. *Returns attention to the ledger, signaling the end of the conversation*

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: *Spins on heel, storming out of the shop, muttering to himself* Capitalist pigs! Exploiting the工人阶级! The工人阶级 will rise! The革命 is inevitable! transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: *Looks up briefly as the door slams, shakes head, and returns to the ledger, dipping pen in ink with a quiet sigh* Another satisfied customer.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
